# Issue #88: A library for other languages (`artifact = "c-library"`)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/88).

`targets`, `ready` · opened 2026-09-30 · updated 2026-10-10 · 9 comments

Owner's order: **second** of the five big pieces (after `std::db`). Record: [ADR-125](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-125.md), all of it. Nothing built.

A `pub extern "C" fn` with a body is an entry point, and `artifact = "c-library"` in `[build]` makes the package a library. What a C caller gets is deliberately narrow: numbers by value; text and bytes in as pointer and length, out into a **buffer the caller owns** (size, capacity, written; a `NULL` buffer asks for the size); a struct as an opaque handle with `_new` and `_free`; an enum as numbered constants; an optional as `NULL` or the package's `NONE`. Every entry point returns an `int` status and puts values in out-parameters; a `throws` variant is a positive code, the library's own failures are the seven negative ones, `<pkg>_last_error` carries site and secondary list. A caller may hand over its allocator before `init`. A panic is caught at the boundary and poisons the library until `shutdown`/`init`. A pausing function is exported blocking and as `_async`. Every handle carries a lock; a re-entrant call on the same thread is a status, not a deadlock. The header is generated from the ledger and carries its hash.

The direction [ADR-124](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-124.md) and [ADR-147](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-147.md) do **not** face: those let a program *call* C, and both are built.

**Order of work (ADR-125 §5):** the parser and the four refusals; the artifact and the safe shape at entry points; the wrapper per entry point; the runtime surface (`set_allocator`, `init`, `shutdown`, `last_error`, `free`, getters); blocking and async forms and the handle lock; the header generator and naming; a library called from a C program in `examples/`, and the test that links it.

Sub-issues carry the pieces that build on it (struct by value, symbol prefix, cancellation/streams, WebAssembly, bindings, the exported-roots analysis). The bare-metal target reuses this library's allocator and baked settings and comes after it.

## Comments

### keywan-ghadami, [2026-10-08](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/88#issuecomment-6059228977)

#### Built so far (0.0.663 `a644cb4`, 0.0.664 `5110b39`)

The record is [ADR-284](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-284.md), into which ADR-125 was merged. ADR-324 D6 changed the spelling to `extern`, without `"C"`.

**Step 1: the parser and the four refusals.**
- `pub extern fn … { body }` parses, and the tree records `is_extern`.
- The four refusals:
  - `NK1237`: an entry point that is not `pub`;
  - `NK1238`: an entry point in a build that makes no library;
  - `NK1239`: a generic entry point, or a trait's method;
  - `NK1240`: a parameter or result that does not cross to C. The help names the shape that does: `ref String` in, `String` out, `ref Array[T]` of a number, a `pub struct` as a handle, a callback written `sync`.

- `[build] artifact = "c-library"` makes `lib<package>.so`, `lib<package>.a` and `<package>.h` in `target/nikaia/c-library/`.

  - a `uint32_t` that is no Unicode scalar is `E_ARGUMENT`;
  - a panic is caught, returns `E_PANICKED`, and poisons the library for every later call (D8).
- The header carries the seven boundary codes and the digest of the ledger it came from (D12).
- `nikaia run` refuses a library, and a library that exports nothing is refused.
- Test: `tests/c_library.rs`. A C program, compiled with `cc` and linked against the shared library, calls every shape, including the poisoning. It is skipped where there is no C compiler.

- `throws` as positive codes, and `last_error`;
- handles for structs;

# Issue #89: A database is reachable: `std::db`, and a driver that checks the SQL while the program is built

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/89).

`libraries`, `note` · opened 2026-09-30 · updated 2026-10-06 · 0 comments

Owner's order: **first** of the five big pieces, since every later demo stores something in it. Records: [ADR-143](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-143.md) (all of it) and [ADR-254](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-254.md) (where the connection goes). Nothing built.

The compiler knows **no SQL**: a dialect is a grammar in a driver package. A grammar declares a result column with `meta::column(name, type)`, the third and last intrinsic of the hybrid binding, and the compiler derives the statement's row type from the columns as it derives the parameter type from the holes. A `dsl` block takes build-time arguments, named, no `;` (`dsl sqlite(schema: app) { … } eod`), resolved from `comptime` values, and the driver's grammar reads the schema with its own DDL grammar and refuses a missing column **at the query**. `std::db` is the protocol only (traits, statement, row values); `sqlite` and the rest are packages. No expression capture, no ORM; `raw(text)` for dynamic SQL. The connection is the statement's subject and is typed by its schema (ADR-254): `by_age.execute(db; min_age: 18)`, and a connection of another schema is refused at the call.

**What was blocking is gone:** running a grammar while the program is built is built ([ADR-177](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-177.md)), and the shape this needs, a flat list of declared columns and parameters, is one of the five that cross. What is left is the driver's own work.

Order of work is in the sub-issues (ADR-143 §5). `examples/fortunes.nika` waits on this and on the HTTP handler work.

**Open question:** how a schema is bound while the program is built (`let app = comptime asset(…)` vs `comptime APP: db::Schema = asset(…)`) is on `docs/open-decisions.md`, recommendation (1), the item form.

**Built:** the runtime before `main`, files on `io_uring`, sockets signalling readiness (D3-D5); a socket in `std` (ADR-198, 0.0.164); the socket layer (ADR-199, 0.0.165); a minimal HTTP/1.1 server with `http::listen` and its caps (ADR-194 D5, 0.0.166; `examples/hello-http` is driven over a real socket by `tests/project.rs`); its parser written in Nikaia as a grammar (0.0.248, `nikaia-std/src/tools/http1.nika`). `nikaia serve` is **cut** ([ADR-200](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-200.md) D1).

**Open** (sub-issues): `rustls` (D2), HTTP/2, the bodies of ADR-058 and ADR-018 D2, and many connections at once (the server handles one at a time today). Also route hashing, which has no target until a server carries routes.

**One piece was answered without the server:** a name the request chose reaching the filesystem is [ADR-108](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-108.md): the root is an argument of the call (`http::File(path, root)`), built for `fs` at 0.0.178.

**Measured before it is built:** `benches/sendfile/` and `docs/history/zero-copy-send.md` price the five ways a file reaches a socket; `mmap` per request is 2.5x worse than plainly reading at 4 KiB, the trap `http::File` would otherwise walk into.

# Issue #91: Self-hosting: Nikaia compiling Nikaia (Stage 1 and Stage 2)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/91).

`selfhosting`, `tools`, `note` · opened 2026-09-30 · updated 2026-10-06 · 0 comments

The owner's instruction is to take self-hosting **as far as it goes**. Records: [ADR-001](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-001.md) D4 (where the road ends), [ADR-250](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-250.md) (how it is walked), [ADR-252](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-252.md) (the tree), [ADR-257](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-257.md) (the checker's types).

**Where it stands** (`scripts/self_hosting.py`, also the README badge): **5.1 %** of the toolchain is Nikaia, about 2 500 of 48 500 lines.

**The road:** a module moves whole, behind its own interface, leaves first; the Rust module stays as the adapter (D1, D2). **Every move is a test of the compiler**, since each found defects the suite had not, and they are fixed in the compiler in the same package, never bent around in the `.nika` (D3). The share is measured and published (D4).

**Moved so far:** *did you mean*, a `dsl` body's parameters, `describe`'s reader, `Fixed`'s hash, the HTML template scan, the ledger's line reader, what `nikaia.toml` may say, **the whole syntax tree** (a `Span` is two `u32`, `Spanned[T]` is generic), the constant fold, `--trust`'s text, and `Ty`/`Shape` plus the ledger's small records.

**Stage 1** is reached when `main`'s pipeline (read, check, lower) runs Nikaia end to end, with Rust left only as adapters to crates (`winnow`, `clap`, `toml`, the file system). **Stage 2** is reached when the lowered compiler lowers its own sources to byte-identical Rust and a test compares the two (D5).

**Remaining rings, in order:** the checker's types and algorithms; the modules that read only the tree and the types (`dsl`, `traits`, `types`, `contracts::*`, `views`, `diagnostics`); then the ones that read everything: `check` (21 k lines), `emit` (13 k), `parser` (3.9 k), `project` (3.2 k).

Sub-issues carry the next steps and the measured costs.

# Issue #94: A target without an operating system (bare metal)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/94).

`targets`, `blocked` · opened 2026-09-30 · updated 2026-10-06 · 0 comments

Owner's order: **fourth**, after the C library (it reuses its allocator and baked settings) and before the HTTP server's second half. Record: [ADR-119](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-119.md). Nothing built (the compiler knows `x86_64-linux`, `aarch64-linux` and `wasm32-unknown`).

A bare-metal target with `user_parallelism` pinned to `no`; `no_std` emission with a target prelude and abort; the target's executor over described crates with interrupts as wakers and `irq::on(vector, fn() sync)`; a heap by default and an `allocation = "startup"` profile over a derived `allocates` column; locks as critical sections; runtime settings baked at build time. Claims no certification.

**Order of work (ADR-119 §5):** the target and the pin; `no_std` emission; the `std` half over described crates; `allocates` and the profile; build-time settings and the deadline; the availability rows and a first program.

# Issue #97: What is left of a type that holds itself (patterns through a box, guards, `null` without allocation)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/97).

`language`, `note` · opened 2026-09-30 · updated 2026-10-06 · 2 comments

Record: [ADR-246](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-246.md) D5. D1-D4 are built (`tests/recursive_types.rs`); three refinements are not, in this order:
1. A pattern that looks inside a boxed part (`Expr::Add(Expr::Num(n), b)`, `NK1193` today) rewritten into a `match` in the arm.
2. A guard that reads a boxed binding before the arm opens it.
3. A nullable field boxed **inside its option**, so a `null` costs no allocation.

# Issue #99: A Nikaia package is found by version (registry, the `nikaia_NAME` prefix through Cargo)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/99).

`tools`, `ready` · opened 2026-09-30 · updated 2026-10-06 · 0 comments

Record: [ADR-103](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/main/docs/specification/adr/adr-103.md). Today a bare version (`http = "1.2"`) is refused: `path = "…"` dependencies only.

`http = "1.2"` becomes `http = { package = "nikaia_http", version = "1.2" }` in the generated `Cargo.toml`; Cargo finds and fetches, the compiler reads `src/*.nika` and `nikaia.contracts` from where the crate landed and emits it as a workspace member as it does a path dependency; a crate under the prefix without both is refused by name. A package's own package dependencies are not followed yet.

**Order of work (ADR-103 §5):** the manifest arm and the rename; resolution through `cargo metadata` and the not-a-Nikaia-package refusal; following a dependency's own manifest in both arms; the stub `Cargo.toml` written by the build so that `cargo publish` is the whole of publishing.

**Evidence:** Part III 13.3's own example; no package in the tree is published yet, so the first one is the test.
